claim: UNFPA estimates that about half a million women and girls across sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, the Arab States region, and Latin America and the Caribbean are living with obstetric fistula and frames the condition as caused by prolonged obstructed labour without timely high-quality medical treatment.
method: Reviewed the UNFPA topic page for burden framing, mechanism, treatment-access barriers, prevention framing, campaign scope, and reported repairs supported by UNFPA.
limitations: This is a global program framing page, not a country-level prevalence dataset.
The half-million estimate is not presented with a confidence interval or country breakdown on the page.
The page does not distinguish first repair need from recurrent, failed, or inoperable cases.

claim: A 2025 BMJ Global Health modelling study estimated roughly 457,000 women ages 15-64 and 386,000 women ages 15-49 living with obstetric fistula in 2020 across 55 low- and middle-income countries targeted by the UNFPA Campaign to End Fistula.

source.title: Global, regional and national estimates of obstetric fistula prevalence

method: Reviewed search-indexed abstract metadata and DOI record for the population, geography, estimate, and uncertainty range; treated the result as burden framing pending full source-inventory verification.
limitations: The estimate is modelled, not a direct count of confirmed untreated cases.
The source date uses the journal issue month because the exact article publication day was not available from the accessed metadata.
The evidence does not by itself identify surgical capacity, case-finding barriers, or sub-national backlog.

claim: A 2024 PLOS ONE systematic review and meta-analysis estimated pooled successful obstetric fistula surgical repair at 77.85 percent across included low- and middle-income country studies.

source.title: Proportions and determinants of successful surgical repair of obstetric fistula in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis

method: Reviewed the PLOS ONE article metadata and abstract for publication date, DOI, scope, included setting type, and pooled repair-success estimate.
limitations: A pooled repair-success estimate does not measure country-level surgical capacity or access.
Study populations are treated patients, not all women living with fistula.
Closure, continence, follow-up, recurrence, and reintegration outcomes may not be measured consistently across included studies.

claim: The 2024 UN Secretary-General report hosted by UNFPA frames obstetric fistula elimination as requiring action across prevention, treatment, social reintegration, and emerging obstacles such as humanitarian crises and climate change.

source.title: Intensifying efforts to end obstetric fistula within a decade: Report of the Secretary-General (A/79/112)

method: Reviewed the UNFPA resource page metadata and description for publication authority, date, scope, and the policy dimensions named in the report summary.
limitations: The resource page summary does not provide a machine-readable country dataset.
Policy recommendations are global and require country-level verification before operational use.
This source does not quantify repair backlog or surgical capacity by geography.

claim: The DHS Analytical Studies No. 17 report documents that earlier surveys used inconsistent fistula symptom questions and presents a standardized module intended to improve population-based measurement, while treating self-reported severe incontinence as a proxy rather than confirmed obstetric fistula.

source.title: Incontinence Data from the Demographic and Health Surveys: Comparative Analysis of a Proxy Measurement of Vaginal Fistula and Recommendations for Future Population-Based Data Collection

method: Reviewed the DHS publication record and abstract, then checked the report's stated critique of sampling, questionnaire construction, and self-reported symptom measurement against the pack's measurement-family requirements.
limitations: The report is methodological and historical; it is not a current country prevalence dataset or a repair-capacity registry.
Self-reported leakage can have low positive predictive value for confirmed fistula and can include non-obstetric causes.
The report cannot separate untreated backlog from continuing incident prevention failure without linked time, diagnosis, referral, and repair records.

claim: Bangladesh's 2026 national annual report aggregates 2019-2024 case-management records from government health systems, fistula centres, NGOs, and development partners, reporting identified cases, surgeries, successful repairs, facility coverage, and rehabilitation activity; these are program-output measures rather than a national untreated-backlog estimate.

source.title: National Annual report on Obstetric Fistula in Bangladesh

method: Reviewed the official publication page for reporting period, contributing systems, case-management numerators, facility coverage, outcome definitions as presented, and the report's stated validation process.
limitations: The report is a program compilation, not a population-based prevalence survey; cases outside participating systems may be missed.
Identified cases, admissions, surgeries, and successful repairs have different numerators and must not be treated as interchangeable.
The public page does not expose patient-level denominators, case-finding sensitivity, recurrence, loss to follow-up, or a complete national facility frame.
The report includes iatrogenic and other fistula categories, so obstetric-fistula totals require type-specific extraction before use.

claim: WHO's emergency obstetric care handbook defines facility signal functions and indicators spanning availability, access, use, and quality, providing a prevention-capacity measurement framework relevant to obstructed-labour risk but not a direct incidence or fistula-backlog measure.

source.title: Monitoring emergency obstetric care: a handbook

method: Reviewed the WHO publication overview and handbook scope for the distinction between theoretical facility capacity and functioning signal functions, then mapped those indicators to the pack's prevention-capacity measurement family.
limitations: The handbook provides indicator definitions and study guidance, not current country or district observations.
EmOC readiness or use is an upstream prevention proxy and does not identify which women developed fistula or who remains untreated.
A facility assessment can miss referral delay, transport failure, informal care, and variation between assessment and service date.

claim: A 2016 Bangladesh Maternal Morbidity Validation Study clinically examined women identified by survey screening and supplied diagnostic values used to correct a nationally representative survey estimate; the study estimated 17,457 women aged 15-64 living with obstetric fistula in Bangladesh, while showing that self-reported symptom positives had a positive predictive value of 31.6% among women aged 15-49.

source.title: Obstetric fistula in Bangladesh: estimates from a national survey with clinical validation correction

method: Reviewed the article's study design, validation-sample methods, diagnostic-value analysis, national-survey adjustment, results, and limitations. Classified it as a clinically validated prevalence-measurement source because it links survey screening to examination by female physicians and applies verification-bias and misclassification corrections; did not treat its prevalence estimate as a direct untreated-backlog or repair-capacity measure.
limitations: The clinical validation sample was drawn from two upazilas in Sylhet and its diagnostic values were applied to the national survey, so external validity of the correction across Bangladesh is an assumption rather than a directly observed national property.
Only 19 obstetric fistula cases were confirmed in the validation sample, leaving substantial uncertainty around diagnostic statistics and the corrected estimates.
The source uses 2016 survey and validation data and does not link prevalent cases to repair history, current untreated status, recurrence, or access to a functioning repair pathway.

The national 15-64 estimate extrapolates the 50-64 age group from the validation study because the national survey interviewed women aged 15-49 for the fistula module; it should not be compared with another age band without adjustment.
The source_date records the September 2022 journal issue month; the evidence record does not assert a more precise publication day.
